name: AutoCAD
summary: The standard for precise 2D drafting: plans, sections, elevations and details.

shortcuts.action: Object snap / Ortho on and off

tips: Draw at real size (1:1) in model space and set the scale in the layout, never by shrinking the drawing.
Keep one layer per kind of object: walls, doors, dimensions, text. It makes line weights and printing easy.
Type commands with the left hand and keep the right hand on the mouse; it is far faster than the ribbon.
withArchHub: Export a floor from the Floor Plan Studio as DXF and open it in AutoCAD, or use Save As > DXF to bring an AutoCAD drawing in.

name: Revit
summary: Building information modelling: one 3D model that produces plans, sections, schedules and quantities.
tips: Set up levels and grids before drawing a single wall; everything else hangs off them.
Model it once, then let views show it: never redraw the same wall in a section.
Use view templates so every plan in the set has the same line weights and visibility.
withArchHub: Sketch the plan and test options quickly in the Floor Plan Studio, export DXF, and link it into Revit as an underlay to model over.

name: Rayon
summary: A browser-based 2D drawing tool for quick, good-looking plans and space planning.
tips: Import a DXF or PDF as a background and trace over it to restyle an existing plan.
Use its styles to switch a plan between technical and presentation looks.
withArchHub: Both work in the browser; exchange drawings between them with DXF.

name: SketchUp
summary: Fast, intuitive 3D modelling by pushing and pulling surfaces. Ideal for early massing.
tips: Make a group or component of every object as soon as you draw it, so shapes do not stick together.
Type a number straight after starting a move or a push/pull to set an exact distance.
Use scenes to save camera views you will want again for renders.
withArchHub: Import a DXF floor plan from the studio and push/pull the walls up to the height you set.

name: Rhino
summary: Precise free-form modelling with curves and surfaces; with Grasshopper, parametric design.

shortcuts.action: Ortho / Grid snap on and off

tips: Rhino is command-driven: start typing a command name (Line, Loft, Sweep1, ExtrudeCrv) and press Enter.
Build clean curves first. A good surface comes from few, well-placed control points.
Keep geometry on named layers from the start; it pays off when exporting or rendering.
withArchHub: The studio's DXF export keeps curved walls as true arcs, so they arrive in Rhino as clean curves.

name: Blender
summary: A free, open-source 3D suite for modelling, rendering and animation.

shortcuts.action: Switch between Object and Edit mode

tips: After G, R or S, press X, Y or Z to lock to an axis, then type a number for an exact amount.
Set the unit system to metric and work at real size so lighting behaves correctly.
withArchHub: Blender can import DXF with its built-in add-on, so studio plans can be the base for a model.

name: D5 Render
summary: Real-time ray-traced rendering with a large asset library, linked live to your modelling software.
bestFor: Live sync with SketchUp, Rhino and Revit
tips: Get the sun angle and one or two key materials right before adding any assets.
Use the live-sync plugin so model changes update without re-importing.
Add people and plants last, and sparingly: they should support the architecture, not hide it.
withArchHub: Plan and test layouts in the studio first; render the 3D model you build from them in D5.

name: Lumion
summary: Rendering focused on landscapes and atmosphere, with big libraries of plants and effects.
tips: Start from one of the built-in styles, then turn effects down rather than up.
Use LiveSync with your modelling software to see changes immediately.
withArchHub: Use the site study and plan from ArchHub to decide the views worth rendering.

name: Enscape
summary: A real-time renderer that runs inside Revit, SketchUp, Rhino and Archicad.
tips: Because it renders the live model, fix problems in the model, not in the render.
Save views in your modelling software so you can return to the same camera.
withArchHub: Enscape works from your Revit, SketchUp or Rhino model built from the studio's plans.

name: Twinmotion
summary: Real-time visualisation built on Unreal Engine, with seasons, weather and animated context.
tips: Use the weather and season sliders to test how the design reads through the year.
Direct Link keeps the scene in step with your modelling software.
withArchHub: Good for showing a whole site: bring the site dimensions and north from the site study.

name: Photoshop
summary: Image editing for post-production of renders, collage elevations and textured plans.
tips: Work with masks and adjustment layers instead of erasing, so every change can be undone later.
Set layers of textures to Multiply over a line drawing to colour a plan or elevation.
Match the light direction of every cut-out person and tree to the sun in the render.
withArchHub: Export a plan as PNG from the studio (try the presentation styles) and finish it in Photoshop.

name: Illustrator
summary: Vector drawing for diagrams, line weights and crisp graphics at any size.
tips: Give diagrams only two or three line weights and one accent colour.
Use Select > Same > Stroke weight to restyle every line of one kind at once.
withArchHub: The studio exports SVG, which opens in Illustrator as editable vector lines.

name: InDesign
summary: Page layout for portfolios, presentation sheets and reports.

shortcuts.action: Fill frame with image, in proportion
Fit image inside frame, in proportion

tips: Set up a column grid and margins on the parent page before placing anything.
Use paragraph styles for headings and captions so the whole portfolio stays consistent.
Link images instead of pasting them, and package the file before sending it to print.
withArchHub: Place PNG or SVG exports from the studio and the concept sketch straight into your sheets.

name: Canva
summary: Quick browser-based layouts from templates: boards, slides and social posts.
tips: Pick one template and strip it back; too many decorative elements weaken architectural work.
Export as PDF Print for boards that will be printed.
withArchHub: Upload plan images and the concept sketch exported from ArchHub into your boards.

name: Midjourney
summary: AI image generation from text, strong at mood, atmosphere and concept imagery.

shortcuts.action: How artistic it is allowed to be (0 to 1000)
How varied the four results are

tips: Describe the building like a photograph: subject, material, light, weather, viewpoint, lens.
It invents architecture: use the images for mood and ideas, never as a record of your design.
withArchHub: The Prompt Builder in AI Studio writes prompts in this format from simple choices.

name: Stable Diffusion
summary: Open AI image generation you can run yourself, and steer closely with your own drawings.
bestFor: Turning a line drawing or massing view into a render

shortcuts.action: List what you do not want (blurry, distorted, text)
How strictly it follows your words
More steps means more refined, and slower
Keep the lines or depth of your drawing exactly

tips: With ControlNet, a clean line export of your elevation keeps the real proportions of your design.
Keep denoising strength low (0.3 to 0.5) to stay close to your original image.
withArchHub: Export a plan or sketch as PNG from ArchHub and use it as the guiding image.

name: ChatGPT
summary: A general AI assistant: useful for writing, research summaries and checking your reasoning.
tips: Give it context first: project type, site, climate, and what you have decided so far.
Ask it to play a critical juror and question your concept; answer out loud as practice.
Always check facts, building codes and dimensions against a real source. It can be confidently wrong.
withArchHub: Download the concept summary as text from the Concept Planner and paste it in as context.
